review_type: single AI curator; full received final answer read; model identity visible

errors.quote: if the Q-time effect survives covariate adjustment, it is not explained by measured movement.
errors.issue: Post-inhibition movement can be a mediator or collider. Adjustment or propensity matching on it does not establish a retrieval-specific direct effect; disappearance likewise does not prove a motor confound. Keep a total-effect analysis and experimentally dissociate motor requirements.

errors.quote: include the R-terminal control which would also show an effect if antidromic spread to the whole P population were the cause
errors.issue: The two terminal fields can differ in opsin density, light coverage and recruited neurons. A null R intervention does not exclude off-Q effects of Q light. Measure relevant P/other-target output under the actual Q illumination.

errors.quote: if both converge, antidromic artifact is unlikely to be the whole story
errors.issue: Somatic inhibition can reproduce the same collateral mechanism as a nonlocal terminal manipulation. Convergence does not independently exclude that common explanation.

errors.quote: necessity is supported only by the *conjunction* of positive Q-time and null comparators.
errors.issue: Several pathways or task epochs can be necessary. Comparator effects need direct interaction estimates and appropriate equivalence bounds; null significance is neither mandatory for pathway necessity nor sufficient for unique retrieval specificity.

errors.quote: record P (soma, for the retrograde design) or Q neuron activity (terminal design)
errors.issue: General Q firing is not necessarily the relevant P-to-Q transmission readout, particularly for inhibitory inputs. Validate pathway-evoked synaptic output, suppression kinetics and recovery; the protocol does not clearly require these.

errors.quote: **Primary outcome:** proportion correct choices, per condition, per animal.
errors.issue: Omissions and aborted trials have no prespecified denominator or analysis. Treatment-dependent response completion can distort the proposed correct/incorrect comparison.

rationale: Correctly prefers Q terminals and includes useful randomization and a movement-matched task idea. However, the central movement-adjustment inference is invalid, other-target and soma controls overexclude shared collateral effects, and omission handling and functional timing remain underspecified. These affect the causal conclusion rather than merely presentation.
reference_guardrails: O1 establishes that population P has two targets, not that every Q-projecting neuron collateralizes. Do not assume either overlap or disjointness; validate or retain the limitation.

Projection-defined somatic inhibition tests a population and all its affected outputs. Local Q-terminal intervention is preferable for a pathway claim but also needs actual transmission and off-target validation.
Suppression in neuronal somata does not guarantee suppression of terminal transmission. Validate physiological onset, sustained effect, offset recovery and rebound at the actual behavioral settings.

Reduced normal performance supports a conditional causal requirement, not memory storage or an exclusive retrieval computation. Cue perception, attention, maintenance and motor preparation remain alternatives.
Light offset is not necessarily inhibition offset. A choice made after light ends can correctly report an earlier retrieval deficit; outcome timing alone is not a rebound diagnosis.
Movement adjustment/matching after intervention and conditioning on response completion can bias inference. Report all randomized trials and use experimental motor/sensory dissociations.
A nonsignificant control effect is not equivalence. Predefine biologically meaningful bounds and obtain enough precision to exclude consequential confounds.
Two pathways or epochs can both be necessary. Effects in an other-projection control do not by themselves invalidate the tested pathway contribution.

Numbers missing from the packet may be proposed as pilot settings; no specific opsin, surgical coordinate or animal count is mandatory. Operational calibration and justified independent-animal sampling are required.

Reference correction: population-level divergence must not be described as demonstrated single-neuron collateralization. Terminal effects on intended local Q signaling are part of the intervention, not automatically an off-target artifact.

review_sources.title: Mahn et al. (2016): biophysical constraints of presynaptic optogenetic inhibition
review_sources.scope: Reviewer-only primary-source check of terminal efficacy, paradoxical release and offset rebound; no particular construct is required by the question.
